target.title: fix(mcp): standalone apps stop hanging on stalled gateway requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where standalone MCP Apps could either hang forever on a stalled Gateway response or reject a healthy tool/resource operation after 30 seconds even though its MCP server allowed a longer request deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

The initial standalone view fetch keeps the existing 30-second Gateway watchdog. A live App view now snapshots a whole-operation deadline from its existing ten-minute lifetime, widened when the owning MCP server's configured request timeout is longer. Each tool or resource operation uses one shared abort signal across catalog refresh, authorization, pagination, and every MCP SDK request; the browser adds the existing 30-second Gateway window only for HTTP response delivery and body consumption. This keeps the deadline stable across `tools/list_changed` cache invalidation and avoids resetting the total budget on each upstream page. Shared catalog refreshes track their live operation waiters: one timed-out caller detaches without cancelling another caller, while the final waiter aborts connection setup and any remaining `tools/list` pages, prevents an aborted catalog from being cached, and lets a later load retry cleanly. Page-close cancellation and the existing ticket, sandbox, and authorization boundaries remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Standalone MCP Apps still fail clearly instead of hanging when Gateway work stalls, while healthy catalog-refresh, paginated resource, and long-running tool operations can complete within the view-owned operation lifetime. Timed-out operations also stop orphaned catalog pagination without disrupting another live operation that is sharing the refresh.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts` — 81/81 passed. The regressions show that catalog pagination stops after the final operation waiter aborts, another live waiter is not cancelled, and a later catalog load starts fresh.
- Six affected standalone App, UI resource, server-method, and MCP consumer test files — 69/69 passed.
- Targeted `oxlint` across the four catalog-refresh runtime and regression-test files — passed.
- Targeted `oxfmt --check` across the same four files — passed.
- Real Chromium + real standalone HTTP host + real stdio MCP SDK server: a 31.5-second tool call with a 45-second per-request MCP deadline reached the App and invoked a follow-up acknowledgement tool 38.037 seconds after the browser opened, beyond the old 30-second watchdog. The view-owned browser deadline was 630 seconds (ten-minute App operation lifetime plus 30 seconds of HTTP/body grace).
- Local `tsgo` could not run because the required cgroup resource envelope was unavailable; current-head CI remains the typecheck authority.
